title: Compatible opens containing rational points exhaust after a finite extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Z$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every finite intermediate extension $k\subseteq K\subseteq\bar k$ (finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space), suppose an open subset $U[K]\subseteq Z_K=Z\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ is given. Assume that every $K$-rational point of $Z_K$ has image in $U[K]$, and that for each inclusion $K\subseteq K'$ the inverse image $(U[K])_{K'}$ is contained in $U[K']$. Then $U[K]=Z_K$ for some finite intermediate extension $K/k$. No separability, perfectness, smoothness or reducedness is assumed.

source.place: Appendix B, Lemma B.36, printed p.604

proof.text: Put $\overline Z=Z_{\bar k}$ and let $p_K:\overline Z\to Z_K$ be the scalar projection. Define $W_K=p_K^{-1}(U[K])$. These are open subsets of the same space $\overline Z$. By finite-type base change, $\overline Z$ is of finite type over $\bar k$, hence quasi-compact by the definition of finite type over an affine base.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type); Milne B.36, alternative algebraic-closure argument, setup

proof.text: Let $x$ be a closed point of $\overline Z$. Since $\bar k$ is algebraically closed and $\overline Z$ is locally of finite type over it, the structural map $\bar k\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse gives a $\bar k$-rational point $q:\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\overline Z$ with image $x$. Compose $q$ with $\overline Z\to Z$ to obtain $a:\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to Z$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points) and Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), algebraically closed specialization

proof.text: Choose from the finite-type affine cover of $Z$ an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing the image of $a$, and write $A=k[a_1,\ldots,a_n]$. The map $a$ on this affine is a $k$-algebra map $\varphi:A\to\bar k$. Every $\varphi(a_i)$ is algebraic over $k$, so $K=k(\varphi(a_1),\ldots,\varphi(a_n))$ is finite over $k$. Since every element of $A$ is a polynomial in the $a_i$ over $k$, $\varphi(A)\subseteq K$. Thus $\varphi$ factors through $A\to K$, giving $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ whose extension to $\bar k$ is $a$. By the fibre-product universal property, $b$ gives a $K$-rational point $b_K$ of $Z_K$, and $p_Kq$ is its composite with $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. By the assumed rational-point inclusion, the image of $b_K$ lies in $U[K]$; consequently $x\in W_K$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated); affine coordinate factorization written out, rather than invoking a point-descent theorem

proof.text: The closed subset $C=\overline Z\setminus\bigcup_K W_K$ contains no closed point of $\overline Z$, by the preceding two steps. Apply the Jacobson statement for schemes locally of finite type over a field: the closed points of $\overline Z$ lying in $C$ are dense in $C$. Here this set is empty, whose closure is empty, so $C=\varnothing$. Hence the $W_K$ cover $\overline Z$.

By quasi-compactness choose $K_1,\ldots,K_r$ with $\overline Z=\bigcup_{i=1}^r W_{K_i}$. Choose a finite $k$-basis of each $K_i$ and let $L\subseteq\bar k$ be the field generated by all these basis elements over $k$. They are algebraic, so $L/k$ is finite. It contains each $K_i$, since it contains its basis and all its $k$-linear combinations. The given compatibility and the composition of scalar projections imply $W_{K_i}\subseteq W_L$. It follows that $W_L=\overline Z$. If the finite subcover is empty, then $\overline Z$ is empty; the same construction means $L=k$ and still $W_L=\overline Z$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated); finite-subcover definition and the assumed monotonicity

proof.text: The field extension $L\subseteq\bar k$ induces a surjection $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. Its base change along $Z_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is $p_L:\overline Z\to Z_L$, so $p_L$ is surjective. For each $z\in Z_L$ choose $y\in\overline Z$ with $p_L(y)=z$. Since $W_L=p_L^{-1}(U[L])=\overline Z$, we have $z\in U[L]$. Therefore $U[L]=Z_L$, as required.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective); elementary detection of equality of subsets by surjective inverse image

proof_origin.place: Appendix B, Lemma B.36, printed p.604 (PDF p.616). Alternative proof via the algebraic closure, affine coordinate descent, the Jacobson property, quasi-compactness, and surjective field base change; this is not Milne's printed dimension-decrease proof.

Proof: it is agent-written and openly not Milne's argument; I checked each of the six steps against the cited statements. (1) Finite-type base change, then the affine-base definition, gives quasi-compactness of Z_kbar. (2) The closed-point residue-field iso over an algebraically closed field gives a section q through each closed point. (3) Affine coordinates of A=k[a_i] map into K=k(phi(a_i)), which is finite by the IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin leaf. I verified p_K∘q = b_K∘j on both fibre-product components, so x lies in W_K. (4) The closed-subset form of the Jacobson leaf forces the closed complement C to be empty. (6) Spec kbar→Spec L is surjective, its base change p_L is surjective, so U[L]=Z_L. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses.
